issues.legal_issue: A concurrent factual finding that a purported partition was sham and not intended to operate is not disturbed in a special-leave appeal when evidence supports it.
material_facts: The lower courts found that the deed was executed to defeat widows’ rights and was not genuine.
The deed did not name or bear the signatures of the persons said to have assisted with the division, divided land unequally, and made no provision for dividing the family house.
The family members continued to possess the lands jointly, live in the same house, and share meals after the deed.
The lower courts’ finding was based on evidence that the Supreme Court found sufficient.
issues.conclusion: The Court upheld the concurrent finding that the partition deed was sham and not intended to be effective; it found no basis to disturb that factual finding in the special-leave appeal.
issues.legal_principle: A concurrent finding of fact is ordinarily accepted in an appeal by special leave. The Court may intervene where the finding is challenged as unsupported by evidence, but the circumstances and evidence here supported the finding.

rule.if: property_partition_appeal and special_leave_appeal and concurrent_factual_finding and evidence_supports_sham_partition

predicates.property_partition_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal arising from a dispute over partition of family property.
predicates.special_leave_appeal: The appeal is brought by special leave.
predicates.concurrent_factual_finding: The trial court and the appellate court reached the same factual finding about the purported partition.
predicates.evidence_supports_sham_partition: The evidence supports a finding that the purported partition was not intended to operate as a genuine division.

issues.definition: When a special-leave appeal in a property partition dispute challenges a concurrent factual finding that is supported by evidence, the finding is upheld.

issues.legal_issue: A purported partition does not sever joint-family status when the expressed intention to separate is merely sham or pretended.
material_facts: The family members relied on the purported partition deed as expressing an intention to separate.
The courts found the deed sham and intended to defeat the widows’ rights, not to effect a genuine separation.
The family members continued in joint possession and continued living and dining together.
issues.conclusion: The sham deed did not sever the joint-family status.
issues.legal_principle: A definite and unambiguous intention by a member to separate, clearly communicated to the other coparceners, can sever joint status without their assent. But an expression of intention that is merely a pretence or sham does not effect severance. The Court relied on Merla Ranumna v. Chelikani Jagannadha Rao and Others.

predicates.property_partition_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal arising from a dispute over partition of family property.
predicates.purported_separation: A family member or members expressed an intention to separate from the joint family.
predicates.sham_intention: The expressed intention to separate was a pretence and was not genuinely meant to divide the family or its property.

issues.definition: Where a purported separation in a property partition dispute was only a pretence, joint-family status is not severed.

issues.legal_issue: A member claiming that acquired property is separate must displace the inference of joint-family ownership that arises when the family had an adequate nucleus capable of funding the acquisition.
material_facts: The family possessed ancestral land measuring 151 acres and 27 gunthas, including irrigated land, and the evidence showed substantial income and resources for cultivation.
Twelve additional parcels were acquired over about thirty years for a total price of Rs. 4,800, which the courts found could have been funded from the family property.
The appellants asserted that the acquisitions were made from separate business income but did not establish the nature or source of that income with reliable evidence.
issues.conclusion: The twelve parcels were joint-family property, and the plaintiff was entitled to a share in them on partition.
issues.legal_principle: Joint-family status alone does not create a presumption that property held by a member is joint property; the person asserting joint ownership initially bears the burden of proof. If an adequate joint-family nucleus is established from which the acquisition could have been made, the burden shifts to the person asserting self-acquisition to prove that the property was acquired without aid from the family estate. The Court relied on Appalaswami v. Suryanarayanamurti and referred to Babubhai Girdharlal v. Ujamlal Hargovandas, Venkataramayya v. Seshamma, and Vythianatha v. Varadaraja.

rule.if: property_partition_appeal and acquired_property_claimed_as_joint and adequate_family_nucleus and nucleus_could_fund_acquisition and no_proof_of_independent_source

predicates.property_partition_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal arising from a dispute over partition of family property.
predicates.acquired_property_claimed_as_joint: A party to the partition dispute claims that property acquired by a family member belongs to the joint family.
predicates.adequate_family_nucleus: The family possessed joint property of sufficient value or productive capacity to provide a financial nucleus.
predicates.nucleus_could_fund_acquisition: The established family nucleus could have provided the means for the acquisition in dispute.
predicates.no_proof_of_independent_source: The party asserting separate ownership did not prove that the acquisition was made from an independent source without aid from the family estate.

issues.definition: In a property partition dispute, acquired property is treated as joint-family property when an adequate family nucleus could have funded it and no independent source is proved.

issues.legal_issue: A challenge to an alienation is sufficiently pleaded when the plaint, read as a whole, contests the alienations and seeks relief concerning the scheduled property that includes the property sold.
material_facts: One paragraph of the plaint did not specifically identify the sale of the two parcels at issue.
Other paragraphs challenged alienations made in favour of the defendants and sought relief concerning all lands listed in the plaint’s schedule.
The two parcels sold were expressly listed in that schedule.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the contention that the plaintiff had not challenged the sale and held that the plaint sufficiently put it in issue.
issues.legal_principle: The plaint must be read as a whole; a claim concerning an alienation need not be confined to one paragraph where the overall pleading challenges the alienations and seeks relief for the property expressly included in the schedule.

predicates.property_partition_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal arising from a dispute over partition of family property.
predicates.plaint_challenges_alienations_generally: The plaint, read as a whole, challenges alienations and seeks relief against them.
predicates.disputed_property_in_schedule: The property affected by the disputed alienation is expressly included in the plaint’s property schedule.

issues.definition: A challenge to an alienation is sufficiently pleaded when the plaint generally contests the alienations and includes the affected property in its schedule.

issues.legal_issue: A sale of family property to a minor is not binding on a claimant to the family property when the sale is found to be without consideration and not genuine.
material_facts: The buyer was a minor when the sale was made.
The seller acted as the minor’s guardian, and the minor had no property of her own.
The High Court found the sale to be without consideration and not genuine.
issues.conclusion: The sale was not binding on the plaintiff.
issues.legal_principle: The Court affirmed the finding that the sale was not genuine and was without consideration, given the circumstances that the buyer was a minor, the seller acted as her guardian, and she had no property of her own. No statute or earlier case was cited for this determination.
